MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:3:/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:4:# Reshuffling products of finitely supported laws
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:5:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:6:The sampling procedure of the sub-line lemma produces its six independent
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:7:generating blocks in one grouping, while the restricted line-point laws that
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:8:the projected marginals must match present the same six blocks in another
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:9:grouping.  This module records the rewriting rules that pass between two such
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:10:presentations: the support and the weight of a product, the fact that a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:11:push-forward along a bijection is determined by the supports and weights it
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:12:compares, and the push-forward of the second factor of a product.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:13:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:14:## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:15:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:16:The rewriting rules support `lem:qld-sublines` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:17:blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:18:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:19:The product operation is that of blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:20:`def:line-point-dist`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:21:-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:31:/-! ## The support and the weight of a product -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:33:/-- The support of a product law is the product of the supports.  Blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:34:`def:line-point-dist`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:35:`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:36:-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:41:/-- The weight of a product law is the product of the weights.  Blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:42:`def:line-point-dist`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:43:`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:44:-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:49:/-! ## Push-forward along a bijection -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:51:/-- A push-forward along a bijection is identified by the supports and the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:52:weights it compares: if the map matches the two supports and carries each
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:53:weight to the corresponding weight, and if it has a two-sided inverse, the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:54:push-forward is the target law.  Blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:55:`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:56:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:94:/-! ## Push-forward of the second factor of a product -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:96:/-- Pushing the second factor of a product forward is pushing the product
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:97:forward along the map acting on that factor alone.  Blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:98:`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineShuffle.lean:99:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:4:/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:5:# The projected marginals of the sub-line law
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:6:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:7:This module identifies the two projected point marginals of the sub-line law
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:8:of `lem:qld-sublines` as mixtures of the restricted product laws.  The two
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:9:source lines of a sampled triple depend on the drawn extended point only
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:10:through the canonical representatives of its two source blocks, and those
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:11:representatives are unchanged when the drawn point is replaced by any point of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:12:the extended line; a uniform point of the extended line through a uniform
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:13:point is a uniform point, so the drawn point may be replaced throughout by the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:14:point that is finally retained.  The six generating blocks of the resulting
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:15:law -- the two source point blocks, the two scalar seeds and the two source
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:16:direction blocks -- are then regrouped into the two restricted product laws
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:17:carried by the two indices of the branch.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:18:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:19:## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:20:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:21:The identification is the last step of the proof of `lem:qld-sublines` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:22:blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:23:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:24:The restricted laws are `def:ith-restricted-line`, blueprint lines
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:25:1209--1228, paper lines 1038--1048.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:26:-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:36:/-! ## Source lines depend on the point block only through its representative -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:38:/-- Two source lines of the same branch with the same seed and the same source

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:58:`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:59:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:92:/-- Replacing the drawn extended point by a point of the extended line does

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:95:`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:96:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:129:/-! ## Generating form of the restricted product components -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:131:/-- The restricted line-point law of a kind at an index is the law of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:132:source line of that kind decoded from a uniform point block, a scalar seed in

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSource.lean:135:`lem:qld-sublines`, paper

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSupport.lean:6:This module rewrites the two restricted line-point laws of

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSupport.lean:8:low-degree vector conditioned on the coordinate-index fiber of its retained

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSupport.lean:13:block inherited from the extended line or from freshly sampled data, and each
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSupport.lean:14:is asserted to follow a restricted law.

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSupport.lean:172:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSupport.lean:190:/-! ## Generating laws of the restricted line-point distributions -/

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSupport.lean:195:of its seed.  This is the generating description used in the sampling

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSupport.lean:223:of its seed.  This is the generating description used in the sampling
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSupport.lean:224:procedure of blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSupport.lean:225:`lem:qld-sublines`, paper

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:3:/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:4:# Uniformity under the identification of the two scalar fields
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:6:The extended line of the sub-line construction lives over the scalar field of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:7:the directly indexed extended game, while the two source lines live over the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:8:scalar field of the Pauli basis test.  The two fields are identified
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:9:coordinatewise by a field isomorphism, so that identification is a bijection
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:10:of the coordinate spaces and therefore carries uniform laws to uniform laws.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:11:This module records that transport for a whole extended point and for the two
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:12:source blocks of an extended point, and it records the resampling rule that
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:13:reading a function at the point of a uniformly random affine parameter on the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:14:line through the canonical representative of a uniformly random point is the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:15:same as reading that function at a uniformly random point.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:16:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:17:## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:18:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:19:The statements support `lem:qld-sublines` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:20:blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:21:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:22:The coordinate blocks are those of `def:combine-map`, blueprint lines
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:23:445--480, paper lines 970--989.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:24:-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:34:/-! ## The identification of the two scalar fields as a bijection -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:36:/-- The coordinatewise identification of the extended scalar field with the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:37:source scalar field on one source block, presented as a bijection.  Blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:38:`def:combine-map`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:39:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:51:/-- The coordinatewise identification of the extended scalar field with the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:52:source scalar field on a whole extended point, presented as a bijection.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:53:Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:54:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:67:/-- The `X` block of a transported extended point is the transport of its `X`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:68:block.  Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:69:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:74:/-- The `Z` block of a transported extended point is the transport of its `Z`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:75:block.  Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:76:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:81:/-! ## Transport of the uniform laws -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:83:/-- A uniformly random extended point transported to the source scalar field
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:84:is uniformly random.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:85:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:93:/-- A uniformly random source block transported to the source scalar field is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:94:uniformly random.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:95:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:102:/-- The two source blocks of a uniformly random extended point, read in the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:103:source scalar field, are independent and uniformly random.  Blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:104:`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:105:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:123:/-! ## Resampling a uniform point along a line -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:125:/-- Reading a function at the point of a uniformly random affine parameter on
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:126:the line through the canonical representative, in a fixed direction, of a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:127:uniformly random point is the same as reading that function at a uniformly
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:128:random point.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:129:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:3:/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:4:# Uniform points of a line and the blocks of a coordinate direction
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:6:This module records the two elementary geometric inputs of the sampling
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:7:procedure of the sub-line lemma.  First, a uniformly random point of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:8:coordinate space is the same thing as a uniformly random canonical
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:9:representative together with a uniformly random affine parameter along the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:10:direction: the map sending a pair to the point at that parameter on the line
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:11:through the representative has constant fibers of size `q`, because the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:12:kernel of the canonical representative map is the span of the direction and
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:13:for the zero direction that map is the identity.  Second, the two coordinate
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:14:blocks of an elementary coordinate direction of the extended space are the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:15:corresponding elementary direction of the source space in the block that
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:16:carries the coordinate, and zero in the other block and at the two scalar
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:17:coordinates.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:18:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:19:## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:20:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:21:The two statements support `lem:qld-sublines` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:22:blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:23:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:24:The canonical representative map is blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:25:`def:line-representative`; the coordinate blocks are those of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:26:blueprint `def:combine-map`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:27:-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:37:/-! ## The canonical representative for the zero direction -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:39:/-- For the zero direction the canonical representative map of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:40:`def:line-representative` is the identity, since the span of the zero vector
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:41:is trivial.  Blueprint `def:line-representative`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:42:`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:143-174`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:43:-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:51:/-! ## Uniform points of a line -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:53:/-- The point at a uniformly random affine parameter on the line through the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:54:canonical representative of a uniformly random point is uniformly random on
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:55:the whole coordinate space.  Every fiber of the parameterization has exactly
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:56:`q` elements: for a nonzero direction the parameter is determined and the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:57:representative varies over a coset of the span of the direction, and for the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:58:zero direction the representative is the point itself and the parameter is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:59:free.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:60:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:123:/-! ## Injectivity of the two block embeddings -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:125:/-- The `X`-block coordinate embedding of `def:combine-map` is injective.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:126:Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:127:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:132:/-- The `Z`-block coordinate embedding of `def:combine-map` is injective.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:133:Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:134:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:139:/-! ## The blocks of an elementary coordinate direction -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:141:/-- The `X` block of the elementary direction at an `X`-block coordinate is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:142:the elementary direction of the source space at that coordinate.  Blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:143:`def:combine-map`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:144:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:152:/-- The `X` block of the elementary direction at a `Z`-block coordinate
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:153:vanishes.  Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper

/-!
# The ordered point product on a single placement

The consistency guarantees carried by the joint point measurement compare it
with the ordered `Z`-then-`X` product across a pair of opposite placements.
The scalar estimates used to combine the two Pauli bases instead need the two
families on one placement.  This module obtains that form by inserting the
joint measurement on the opposite placement and applying the squared-distance
triangle inequality twice.

## References

The statement is `lem:qld-4-10-same-placement` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`; it restates the ordered
`Z`-then-`X` display of `lem:qld-4-10`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:689-709`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
open MIPStarRE.Quantum

noncomputable section

/-- Every placement has an opposite placement, and the relation is symmetric
between the two members of each pair. -/
theorem Placement.exists_isOpposite (p : Placement) :
    ∃ q : Placement, p.IsOpposite q ∧ q.IsOpposite p := by
  cases p with
  | AA' => exact ⟨.BA'', trivial, trivial⟩
  | BA'' => exact ⟨.AA', trivial, trivial⟩
  | BB' => exact ⟨.AB'', trivial, trivial⟩
  | AB'' => exact ⟨.BB', trivial, trivial⟩

/-- On a single placement, the joint point measurement is close to the ordered
`Z`-then-`X` point product, with inflation factor four. -/
theorem CombinedPointsWitness.orderedZX_dist_le {P : AdmissibleParams}
    {ε δ : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P ε}
    (points : CombinedPointsWitness S δ) (p : Placement) :
    opFamilyDistSq
        (uniformDistribution
          ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)))
        (fun xz ab => S.place p ((points.Q p.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
        (fun xz ab => S.place p
          ((S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
            (S.pointMeasExp p.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
        S.psiHat ≤ 4 * δ := by
  obtain ⟨q, hpq, hqp⟩ := p.exists_isOpposite
  have htri := opFamilyDistSq_le_of_le_of_le
    (uniformDistribution
      ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)))
    (fun xz ab => S.place p ((points.Q p.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
    (fun xz ab => S.place q ((points.Q q.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
    (fun xz ab => S.place p
      ((S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
        (S.pointMeasExp p.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
    S.psiHat δ δ (points.self_consistent p q hpq)
    (points.consistent_ZX q p hqp)
  linarith

end

end MIPStarRE.QPBT

The first scalar estimate in the combining argument samples an extended line
from the sub-line witness and then a uniform affine parameter on that line.
This module records that the resulting extended point is uniform and hence
that its two source coordinate blocks are independent uniform points.

/-- A dependent mixture of a constant family is the constant law. -/
private theorem Distribution.bind_const_current {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    (μ : Distribution α) (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (ν : Distribution β) :
    Distribution.bind μ (fun _ => ν) = ν := by
  have hne : μ.support.Nonempty := by
    rw [← Finset.card_pos]
    by_contra hcard
    have hempty : μ.support = ∅ := by
      rw [← Finset.card_eq_zero]
      omega
    have htotal := hμ.weight_sum_eq_one
    rw [hempty] at htotal
    simp at htotal
  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
  · change μ.support.biUnion (fun _ => ν.support) = ν.support
    ext b
    simp only [Finset.mem_biUnion]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨a, -, hb⟩
      exact hb
    · intro hb
      obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hne
      exact ⟨a, ha, hb⟩
  · funext b
    change (∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * ν.weight b) = ν.weight b
    rw [← Finset.sum_mul, hμ.weight_sum_eq_one, one_mul]

/-- If every slice of a map of a pair carries the second uniform law to one
fixed law, then the map carries the uniform law of the pair to that law. -/
theorem uniformDistribution_map_uncurry {α β γ : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] [DecidableEq γ]
    (g : α × β → γ) (ν : Distribution γ)
    (hg : ∀ a, (uniformDistribution β).map (fun b => g (a, b)) = ν) :
    (uniformDistribution (α × β)).map g = ν := by
  rw [← bind_uniformDistribution_map (fun a b => g (a, b)),
    show (fun a => (uniformDistribution β).map (fun b => g (a, b))) =
      fun _ => ν from funext hg]
  exact Distribution.bind_const_current _ (uniformDistribution_isProbability α) ν

/-- For the zero direction, the canonical representative map is the identity. -/
private theorem lineRepMap_zero_apply_current {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    (u : Fin m → K) : lineRepMap (0 : Fin m → K) u = u := by
  have hspan : Submodule.span K ({0} : Set (Fin m → K)) = ⊥ := by simp
  have h := sub_lineRepMap_mem_span (0 : Fin m → K) u
  rw [hspan, Submodule.mem_bot, sub_eq_zero] at h
  exact h.symm

/-! ## The Cauchy--Schwarz inequality weighted by a positive operator -/

/-- For a positive operator `A`, the sesquilinear form `⟨u, A v⟩` satisfies the
Cauchy--Schwarz inequality with the two diagonal values `⟨u, A u⟩` and
`⟨v, A v⟩`.  This is the inequality behind the Cauchy--Schwarz steps of the
proofs of `lem:claim-17-2` and `lem:claim-17-3`, in which both factors carry
the square root of the line effect, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1168-1209`. -/
theorem norm_inner_applyOperatorToState_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt {ι : Type*}
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {A : Op ι} (hA : 0 ≤ A)
    (u v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    ‖inner ℂ u (applyOperatorToState A v)‖ ≤
      Real.sqrt (inner ℂ u (applyOperatorToState A u)).re *
        Real.sqrt (inner ℂ v (applyOperatorToState A v)).re := by
  set R : Op ι := CFC.sqrt A with hR
  have hRnonneg : 0 ≤ R := CFC.sqrt_nonneg A
  have hRR : R * R = A := CFC.sqrt_mul_sqrt_self A hA
  have hRherm : Rᴴ = R :=
    (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp hRnonneg).isHermitian.eq
  have hadjoint : (Matrix.toEuclideanLin R).adjoint = Matrix.toEuclideanLin R := by
    rw [← Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_eq_adjoint, hRherm]
  have hsplit : ∀ w z : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι,
      inner ℂ w (applyOperatorToState A z) =
        inner ℂ (applyOperatorToState R w) (applyOperatorToState R z) := by
    intro w z
    have h := LinearMap.adjoint_inner_right (Matrix.toEuclideanLin R) w
      (Matrix.toEuclideanLin R z)
    rw [hadjoint] at h
    rw [← hRR, applyOperatorToState_mul]
    exact h
  have hnorm : ∀ w : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι,
      ‖applyOperatorToState R w‖ =
        Real.sqrt (inner ℂ w (applyOperatorToState A w)).re := by
    intro w
    have h2 : ‖applyOperatorToState R w‖ ^ 2 =
        (inner ℂ (applyOperatorToState R w) (applyOperatorToState R w)).re := by
      rw [@norm_sq_eq_re_inner ℂ]
      rfl
    rw [hsplit, ← h2, Real.sqrt_sq (norm_nonneg _)]
  rw [hsplit, ← hnorm, ← hnorm]
  exact norm_inner_le_norm _ _

/-- The sum over outcomes of the real parts of `⟨u a, A a (v a)⟩`, for
positive weights `A a`, is bounded by the product of the square roots of the
two diagonal sums. -/
theorem abs_sum_re_inner_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt {α ι : Type*} [Fintype α]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : α → Op ι) (hA : ∀ a, 0 ≤ A a)
    (u v : α → EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    |∑ a, (inner ℂ (u a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (v a))).re| ≤
      Real.sqrt (∑ a, (inner ℂ (u a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (u a))).re) *
        Real.sqrt (∑ a, (inner ℂ (v a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (v a))).re) := by
  have hu : ∀ a, 0 ≤ (inner ℂ (u a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (u a))).re :=
    fun a => stateQForm_nonneg (u a) (hA a)
  have hv : ∀ a, 0 ≤ (inner ℂ (v a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (v a))).re :=
    fun a => stateQForm_nonneg (v a) (hA a)
  calc
    |∑ a, (inner ℂ (u a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (v a))).re|
        ≤ ∑ a, |(inner ℂ (u a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (v a))).re| :=
      Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _
    _ ≤ ∑ a, Real.sqrt (inner ℂ (u a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (u a))).re *
          Real.sqrt (inner ℂ (v a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (v a))).re := by
      refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun a _ => ?_
      exact (Complex.abs_re_le_norm _).trans
        (norm_inner_applyOperatorToState_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt (hA a) (u a) (v a))
    _ ≤ Real.sqrt (∑ a,
            Real.sqrt (inner ℂ (u a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (u a))).re ^ 2) *
          Real.sqrt (∑ a,
            Real.sqrt (inner ℂ (v a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (v a))).re ^ 2) :=
      Real.sum_mul_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt _ _ _
    _ = _ := by
      rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => Real.sq_sqrt (hu a),
        Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => Real.sq_sqrt (hv a)]

\section{Repairs and current status}

\paragraph{Direct index sampling (soundness established).}
For arbitrary $m' \ge 1$, the formalization defines the line-point
distribution over $\F_q^{m'}$ by sampling the point, the axis index
$i \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$, and the diagonal direction with vanishing first
$i-1$ coordinates directly.  In the resulting game, line questions carry
the index $i$ (and, for diagonal lines, the projected direction) in place
of the seed $s \in \F_q$.  Soundness form~4 is established for this game
through the low individual degree theorem and the general-simultaneity
combining reduction analysed in \cite{gap:qpbt_ld-simultaneous-sandwich}.
This removes the divisibility obstruction for the
auxiliary directly indexed game.  Because the proof does not use the
tensor-code import, it leaves both original import obligations open rather
than establishing them.

The relation to the present game when $m' \mid q$ must be proved at the level
of strategies, not merely of question distributions.  An
$\mathsf{ALine}$ question of the $\chi$-based game is a pair $(u_0,s)$ and a
$\mathsf{DLine}$ question is a triple $(u_0,s,v')$, so measurements may vary
between seeds in the same class $\chi^{-1}(i)$.  Each seed nevertheless has a
unique decomposition into its index $i$ and a residue
$\rho\in\{0,\ldots,q/m'-1\}$.  The seed-indexed question law is thereby
identified with the direct question law together with a uniform residue; the
parsing map back to the direct question law is an exact pushforward.

The formal transport retains, rather than averages away, the dependence on
$\rho$.  It adjoins a register of dimension $q/m'$ to each player's Hilbert
space, places the two registers in a maximally correlated state, and makes
each question measurement block diagonal, with the block at $\rho$ equal to
the original measurement for the corresponding seed.  Thus both players see
the same residue on a synchronicity branch.  This correlated-residue lift
preserves normalization and projectivity and preserves the game value exactly,
branch by branch.  In particular, seed-dependent relabellings cause no loss;
the earlier obstruction arose only from independently averaging the local
measurements, which is not the construction used here.%
\footnote{The exact distribution comparison is formalized in
\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/Correspondence.lean}.
The lift, projectivity theorem, and value identity are
\leanid{ldStrategyToDirect},
\leanid{ldStrategyToDirect\_isProjective}, and
\leanid{ldStrategyToDirect\_value\_eq} in
\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/SeedFiber.lean} and
\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/SeedFiberValue.lean}.}

Applying form~4 to the lifted strategy produces polynomial-tuple POVMs
$G^{\mathrm A}$ and $G^{\mathrm B}$ on the enlarged carriers.  Compress one
such POVM by taking the normalized average of its diagonal residue blocks.
When the other family is a point measurement, it is constant on the opposite
residue register, and this compression preserves the associated defect
exactly.  Consequently the point/polynomial and polynomial/point conclusions
of the directly indexed theorem transport back to the original seed-indexed
strategy with no additional error.%

\leanid{ldStrategyToDirect\_pointPolynomial\_compression} and
\leanid{ldStrategyToDirect\_polynomialPoint\_compression} in

/-!
# The projected mixtures of the sub-line law

This module assembles the two projected point marginals of the sub-line law of
`lem:qld-sublines` into mixtures of the restricted product laws.  Drawing a
uniform point of the extended line of a mixture of line laws is the same
mixture of the corresponding uniform-point laws, so the two projected
marginals of the sub-line law are the mixtures, over the drawn kind and the
drawn extended coordinate, of the projected marginals of one branch at one
extended coordinate.  Each of those is the component law of the pair of
indices carried by that branch, so the mixing law is the law of the kind
together with the pair of indices assigned to a uniform extended coordinate.

## References

The assembly is the last step of the proof of `lem:qld-sublines` in
blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
The restricted laws are `def:ith-restricted-line`, blueprint lines
1209--1228, paper lines 1038--1048.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT

noncomputable section

/-! ## The uniform point of a mixture of line laws -/

/-- Drawing a uniform point of the extended line of a mixture of line-triple
laws is the corresponding mixture of the uniform-point laws.  Blueprint
`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
theorem subLinePointDist_bind (P : AdmissibleParams) {α : Type*}
    (μ : Distribution α) (ν : α → Distribution (SubLineTriple P)) :
    subLinePointDist P (Distribution.bind μ ν) =
      Distribution.bind μ (fun a => subLinePointDist P (ν a)) := by
  classical
  unfold subLinePointDist
  rw [Distribution.prod_bind_left, Distribution.bind_map]

/-! ## The projected marginals of one branch at one extended coordinate -/

/-- One branch of the sampling procedure, read at a fixed extended coordinate,
is the law of the triple decoded from the auxiliary randomness of that
coordinate.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
theorem subLineBranchDist_eq_bind (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind) :
    subLineBranchDist P kind =
      Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2))) fun k =>
        (Distribution.prod (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P))
            (Distribution.prod (subLineSeedDist P (subLineXIndex P k))
              (subLineSeedDist P (subLineZIndex P k)))).map
          fun w => subLineTripleOf P kind k w := by
  classical
  rw [subLineBranchDist, subLineRawDist, Distribution.bind_map]
  refine Distribution.bind_congr_support _ _ _ fun k _ => ?_
  rw [Distribution.map_map]

/-- The `X` marginal of a uniform point of the extended line of one branch at
one extended coordinate is the `X` component law of the pair of indices of
that branch.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
theorem subLineBranchDist_map_subLineXProjection_at (P : AdmissibleParams)
    (kind : LineKind) (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) :
    (subLinePointDist P
        ((Distribution.prod (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P))
            (Distribution.prod (subLineSeedDist P (subLineXIndex P k))
              (subLineSeedDist P (subLineZIndex P k)))).map
          fun w => subLineTripleOf P kind k w)).map subLineXProjection =
      subLineXComponentDist P
        (kind, (subLineXIndex P k, subLineZIndex P k)) := by
  classical
  unfold subLinePointDist
  rw [Distribution.prod_map_left, Distribution.map_map, Distribution.map_map]
  exact subLineBranchRaw_map_projX P kind k

/-- The `Z` marginal of a uniform point of the extended line of one branch at
one extended coordinate is the `Z` component law of the pair of indices of
that branch.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
theorem subLineBranchDist_map_subLineZProjection_at (P : AdmissibleParams)
    (kind : LineKind) (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) :
    (subLinePointDist P
        ((Distribution.prod (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P))
            (Distribution.prod (subLineSeedDist P (subLineXIndex P k))
              (subLineSeedDist P (subLineZIndex P k)))).map
          fun w => subLineTripleOf P kind k w)).map subLineZProjection =
      subLineZComponentDist P
        (kind, (subLineXIndex P k, subLineZIndex P k)) := by
  classical
  unfold subLinePointDist
  rw [Distribution.prod_map_left, Distribution.map_map, Distribution.map_map]
  exact subLineBranchRaw_map_projZ P kind k

/-! ## The mixing law of the two indices -/

/-- The law of the kind and the pair of source indices assigned to a uniform
extended coordinate of one branch.  Blueprint
`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
noncomputable def subLineComponentBranch (P : AdmissibleParams)
    (kind : LineKind) : Distribution (SubLineComponent P) :=
  (uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2))).map fun k =>
    (kind, (subLineXIndex P k, subLineZIndex P k))

/-- The mixing law of the sub-line lemma: the equal mixture over the two kinds
of the law of the pair of source indices of a uniform extended coordinate.
Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
noncomputable def subLineComponentDist (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    Distribution (SubLineComponent P) :=
  Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (Fin 2))
    ![subLineComponentBranch P .axis, subLineComponentBranch P .diagonal]

/-- The mixing law has total mass one. -/
theorem subLineComponentDist_isProbability (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    (subLineComponentDist P).IsProbability := by
  refine Distribution.bind_isProbability _ _
    (uniformDistribution_isProbability _) fun c _ => ?_
  fin_cases c
  · exact Distribution.IsProbability.map
      (uniformDistribution_isProbability _) _
  · exact Distribution.IsProbability.map
      (uniformDistribution_isProbability _) _

/-! ## The two projected marginals of one branch -/

/-- The `X` marginal of a uniform point of the extended line of one branch is
the mixture, along the pair of source indices of a uniform extended
coordinate, of the `X` component laws.  Blueprint
`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
theorem subLineBranchDist_map_subLineXProjection (P : AdmissibleParams)
    (kind : LineKind) :
    (subLinePointDist P (subLineBranchDist P kind)).map subLineXProjection =
      Distribution.bind (subLineComponentBranch P kind)
        (subLineXComponentDist P) := by
  classical
  rw [subLineBranchDist_eq_bind, subLinePointDist_bind, Distribution.bind_map,
    subLineComponentBranch, Distribution.bind_map_left]
  refine Distribution.bind_congr_support _ _ _ fun k _ => ?_
  exact subLineBranchDist_map_subLineXProjection_at P kind k

/-- The `Z` marginal of a uniform point of the extended line of one branch is
the mixture, along the pair of source indices of a uniform extended
coordinate, of the `Z` component laws.  Blueprint
`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
theorem subLineBranchDist_map_subLineZProjection (P : AdmissibleParams)
    (kind : LineKind) :
    (subLinePointDist P (subLineBranchDist P kind)).map subLineZProjection =
      Distribution.bind (subLineComponentBranch P kind)
        (subLineZComponentDist P) := by
  classical
  rw [subLineBranchDist_eq_bind, subLinePointDist_bind, Distribution.bind_map,
    subLineComponentBranch, Distribution.bind_map_left]
  refine Distribution.bind_congr_support _ _ _ fun k _ => ?_
  exact subLineBranchDist_map_subLineZProjection_at P kind k

/-! ## The two projected marginals of the sub-line law -/

/-- The `X` point marginal of the sub-line law is the mixture of the `X`
component laws along the mixing law.  Blueprint
`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
theorem subLineDist_map_subLineXProjection (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    (subLinePointDist P (subLineDist P)).map subLineXProjection =
      Distribution.bind (subLineComponentDist P) (subLineXComponentDist P) := by
  classical
  rw [subLineDist, subLinePointDist_bind, Distribution.bind_map,
    subLineComponentDist, Distribution.bind_bind]
  refine Distribution.bind_congr_support _ _ _ fun c _ => ?_
  fin_cases c
  · exact subLineBranchDist_map_subLineXProjection P .axis
  · exact subLineBranchDist_map_subLineXProjection P .diagonal

/-- The `Z` point marginal of the sub-line law is the mixture of the `Z`
component laws along the mixing law.  Blueprint
`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
theorem subLineDist_map_subLineZProjection (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    (subLinePointDist P (subLineDist P)).map subLineZProjection =
      Distribution.bind (subLineComponentDist P) (subLineZComponentDist P) := by
  classical
  rw [subLineDist, subLinePointDist_bind, Distribution.bind_map,
    subLineComponentDist, Distribution.bind_bind]
  refine Distribution.bind_congr_support _ _ _ fun c _ => ?_
  fin_cases c
  · exact subLineBranchDist_map_subLineZProjection P .axis
  · exact subLineBranchDist_map_subLineZProjection P .diagonal

/-- The two one-point projected marginals of the sub-line law are mixtures of
the restricted product laws along one common mixing law.  Blueprint
`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
theorem subLineDist_source_mixture (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    ∃ components : Distribution (SubLineComponent P),
      components.IsProbability ∧
        (subLinePointDist P (subLineDist P)).map subLineXProjection =
          Distribution.bind components (subLineXComponentDist P) ∧
        (subLinePointDist P (subLineDist P)).map subLineZProjection =
          Distribution.bind components (subLineZComponentDist P) :=
  ⟨subLineComponentDist P, subLineComponentDist_isProbability P,
    subLineDist_map_subLineXProjection P,
    subLineDist_map_subLineZProjection P⟩

end

theorem abs_overlap_gap_le_sqrt_of_opFamilyDistSq {X α ι : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (μ : Distribution X) (A : X → Measurement α ι) (B C : X → α → Op ι)
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1)

3:/-!
4:# Evaluation of line polynomials at a sampled point
5:
6:This module records the elementary calculus of the partial evaluation
7:`evalOpt` of a coefficient-list line polynomial at a point: the evaluation of
8:a sum is the sum of the evaluations whenever both summands evaluate, a summand
9:of an evaluating sum evaluates whenever the other summand does, the value is
10:unique, and nothing evaluates at a point off the line. These facts underlie
11:the manipulation of the evaluation classes in items 2 and 3 of the
12:expanded-line consistency lemma.
13:
14:Every declaration below is a formalization-only auxiliary: the source uses
15:these facts about evaluation without stating them.
16:
17:## References
18:
19:The evaluation classes `[eval_u(·) = a]` are `def:ideg-deg-polynomials`, paper
20:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:51-58`. They are
21:manipulated in `eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons` and `eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2`,
22:paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`.
23:-/
31:/-- Coefficient-list evaluation is additive in the coefficient list. This
32:is the additivity behind the convolution of `def:expanded-line-measurement`. -/
40:/-- A line polynomial has at most one value at a point of the line: if it
41:evaluates both to `a` and to `b`, then `a = b`. -/
48:/-- The sum of two evaluating line polynomials evaluates to the sum of
49:their values. This is why the convolution outcome `f = f' + f''` evaluates
50:whenever both convolution factors do. -/
57:/-- If a sum and its second summand evaluate, the first summand evaluates to
58:the difference of their values. This is the converse direction used to identify
59:the convolution fibers of an evaluation class. -/
69:/-- The partial evaluation returns `some a` exactly when the polynomial
70:evaluates to `a`. This is the characterization that makes `evalOpt` the total
71:form of the evaluation classes of `def:ideg-deg-polynomials`. -/
86:/-- The partial evaluation returns `none` exactly when no value is
87:determined. This is the outcome that completes the evaluation classes to a
88:measurement, written `[eval_u(·) = ⊥]` in `def:ideg-deg-polynomials`. -/
95:/-- The partial evaluation of a sum of two evaluating line polynomials is
96:the sum of their values. -/
105:/-- If a sum and its second summand evaluate, so does the first summand,
106:with the difference of the two values. -/
115:/-- A point at which some line polynomial evaluates lies on the line. -/
121:/-- Off the line, no line polynomial evaluates, so every outcome falls in
122:the `none` class. -/

## Findings

- [ ] F1 (blocker) `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1590` — Claim 17-1 is marked formalized for the source distribution, but Lean uses the distinct direct-index distribution.

## Review

**F1: Distribution mismatch.** The blueprint fixes \(D\) as the source distribution at `ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1531`. In contrast, `Claims.lean:345` assumes `SubLineWitness`, whose `extended_marginal` explicitly uses `directLinePointDist` (`Witnesses.lean:265`). Its documentation identifies this as an auxiliary replacement, not the source statement. The new uniform-point entry at blueprint line 1574 has the same unstated distinction. State and mark the direct-index results separately; leave the source-labelled claim unmarked until the distributional comparison is supplied. The completed direct-index Claim 17-3 can likewise be recorded separately without marking its unmatched source entry.

**F2: Proof mismatch.** Blueprint lines 1632–1635 use \(W^2\), bound its expectation by \(\delta_Q\), and conclude \(\sqrt{\delta_Q}\). The ordered product need not be Hermitian, so the squared norm uses \(W^\dagger W\). Moreover, `OrderedPoints.lean:45` supplies the same-placement bound \(4\delta_Q\), and `Claims.lean:378` chooses constant \(2\). Update the proof to use \(W^\dagger W\), the opposite-placement insertion, and \(2\sqrt{\delta_Q}\). The big-O statement need not change.

**F3: Combined-point synchronization.** The blueprint proof beginning at `ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:847` still uses binary refinements, quantum linearity, and unresolved ancilla absorption. The new proof instead orthonormalizes the field-valued sandwich on the original local spaces, as explained at `Points.lean:56`. Replace or clearly distinguish the obsolete proof, update its `\uses`, and add proof-level `\leanok`.

**F4: Restricted-distribution status.** The entries at blueprint lines 1251 and 1271 remain `\notready`, and the mixture lemma’s proof lacks `\leanok`. This PR completes normalization, the mixture identities, both inflation estimates, and the restricted consistency bound. Synchronize these entries with the completed results; this does not justify marking the still-open combined-line construction complete.

**F5: Readiness versus completeness.** The new blueprint statement matches the quantified obligation at `Lines.lean:53`, including dependence on the prescribed point-error function. Its missing proof does not make its statement unready. Remove `\notready`, retaining the separate `\lean` link and explicit open-obligation explanation without adding `\leanok`.

**F6: Missing construction links.** Neither `ProjectiveSetting.combinedLineMeasurement` nor `combinedLineMeasurement_sum_Z` appears in the blueprint links. Add a definition/support entry for the concrete POVM and a lemma stating \(\sum_{f_Z}T_{f_X,f_Z}=\hat M^X_{f_X}\), with appropriate completed-status tags and dependencies. Keep these separate from the unfinished consistency obligation.

**F7: Fiber explanation.** For nonzero direction, the canonical representative is fixed throughout a coset. The \(q\)-element fibers belong to \((w,t)\mapsto L_v(w)+tv\) with \(w\) ranging over the entire ambient space, as in `UniformLinePoint.lean:83`. Replace “the representative varies over a coset” with “the sampled ambient point varies over a coset with fixed canonical representative”; clarify the map similarly at blueprint line 1583.

**F8: Prose.** Replace “which belongs to another packet” with “in the low-degree game module,” or drop that clause. The issue reference can remain; this finding concerns terminology, not duplication or modularity.

Summary: three mathematical correspondence/exposition issues, four status/link issues, and one terminology issue. F1 is the principal equivalence blocker.
